test_cases.name: basic_publish_flow
test_cases.prompt: Publish my schliff skill to GitHub

assertions.description: Generates a README for the repo
Does not use the fake install-skill command

test_cases.name: repo_structure_validation
test_cases.prompt: Create a GitHub repo structure for publishing my skill

assertions.description: Does not use the fake install-skill command
Does not include test plan section in PR body for doc-only PRs

test_cases.name: client_data_audit
test_cases.prompt: Publish this skill that was built from a client engagement

assertions.description: Warns about client data in git history
Lists specific data types to scan for
Warns about client data in visual assets

test_cases.name: update_existing_repo
test_cases.prompt: Update my already-published skill with the latest SKILL.md changes

test_cases.name: screenshot_generation
test_cases.prompt: Publish my skill that generates HTML diagnostics — include screenshots

assertions.description: Mentions cleanup of node_modules before committing
Uses a generic demo scenario, not client-specific

test_cases.name: threshold_verification
test_cases.prompt: Publish my ML feature selection skill that uses gain ratio >0.3 and AUC >0.005 thresholds

assertions.description: Verifies threshold claims against published sources
Identifies that gain ratio uses ranking, not fixed cutoffs
Still produces a README alongside verification

test_cases.name: portability_check
test_cases.prompt: Publish this skill that references Snowflake SCD tables and APPLICATION_VERSION_VALID_FROM columns

assertions.description: Suggests using placeholder names instead of real column names
Recommends describing patterns by what they solve, not specific tools

test_cases.name: review_panel
test_cases.prompt: Publish my skill and run a thorough review before pushing

assertions.description: Invokes or suggests multi-agent review panel

test_cases.name: link_verification
test_cases.prompt: Publish my skill — make sure all links in the README work

assertions.description: Checks for correct attribution (upstream vs fork)
Uses a method to actually check link validity

test_cases.name: hook_bundling
test_cases.prompt: Publish my git-squash skill that should auto-trigger after commits

assertions.description: Advises merging with existing hooks, not replacing

test_cases.name: version_bump_completeness
test_cases.prompt: Bump my published skill from v1.0 to v2.0 and push the update

assertions.description: Verifies no stale version strings remain

edge_cases.name: no_skill_md_found
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Reports that the SKILL.md was not found and asks the user to provide the correct path

edge_cases.name: skill_with_no_frontmatter
edge_cases.prompt: Publish this skill — the SKILL.md has no frontmatter (no name or description)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Detects missing frontmatter and either generates it or asks the user for name/description

edge_cases.name: huge_skill_md
edge_cases.prompt: Publish this skill — the SKILL.md is 5000 lines long with extensive methodology
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Proceeds with publishing but may suggest splitting or using progressive disclosure in the README

assertions.description: Still generates README despite large source
Suggests managing content length in README

edge_cases.name: repo_already_exists
edge_cases.prompt: Publish my skill to GitHub but the repo already exists with different content
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Detects existing repo and offers to update rather than create, or suggests force-push with caution

assertions.description: Does not blindly try to create a duplicate repo

edge_cases.name: skill_with_sensitive_data
edge_cases.prompt: Publish this skill — it contains references to Acme Corp and $2.3M revenue figures
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Triggers the client data audit and blocks publishing until sanitization is complete

assertions.description: Identifies the specific sensitive data found
Warns about data in git history

edge_cases.name: no_github_cli
edge_cases.prompt: Publish my skill but I don't have gh CLI installed
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Detects missing gh CLI and suggests installation or manual GitHub workflow

assertions.description: Provides fallback workflow without gh CLI

edge_cases.name: unicode_skill_name
edge_cases.prompt: Publish my skill named 'analyse-donnees' with accented characters in the content
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Handles unicode in skill name and content without errors

edge_cases.name: empty_skill_md
edge_cases.prompt: Publish this skill — the SKILL.md only has a frontmatter block with name and description, no body content
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Warns that the skill has no methodology content and suggests adding substance before publishing

edge_cases.name: fork_contributor_permissions
edge_cases.prompt: Publish my skill by contributing to someone else's repo via a fork PR
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Recognizes that fork contributors cannot set topics or use gh repo edit, and suggests including topics in PR description instead

assertions.description: Suggests workaround for setting topics via PR description

edge_cases.name: multiple_skills_batch
edge_cases.prompt: Publish three of my skills at once — ai-trust-evaluation, agent-review-panel, and publish-skill
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Handles each skill individually with distinct repo names, marketplace identifiers, and no namespace collisions

assertions.description: Treats each skill as a distinct publishing workflow
Ensures unique marketplace identifiers per skill

edge_cases.name: network_failure_mid_publish
edge_cases.prompt: I started publishing but the git push failed halfway — the repo was created but has no content
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Recognizes partial state and suggests recovery (push again or delete and recreate)

edge_cases.name: yaml_frontmatter_conflict
edge_cases.prompt: Publish this skill — the SKILL.md body contains triple-dash --- separators in the methodology section
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Parses frontmatter correctly without confusing body content triple-dashes as frontmatter delimiters

assertions.description: Handles triple-dash in body content correctly

edge_cases.name: marketplace_name_collision
edge_cases.prompt: Publish my skill but the marketplace.json name 'wan-huiyan-publish-skill' is already taken by another plugin
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Detects or warns about potential name collision and suggests a unique identifier

edge_cases.name: skill_with_hooks_already
edge_cases.prompt: Publish my skill — it already has a hooks/ directory with custom hook scripts
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Preserves existing hooks and integrates them into the published repo structure without overwriting

edge_cases.name: repo_not_owned_by_user
edge_cases.prompt: Update the published skill but the GitHub repo is owned by my organization, not my personal account
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Recognizes org-owned repos may have different permission models and adjusts workflow accordingly

edge_cases.name: puppeteer_not_available
edge_cases.prompt: Publish my visual skill but puppeteer is not installed and npm is unavailable
edge_cases.expected_behavior: Skips screenshot generation gracefully and notes the gap in the README

assertions.description: Still generates the README without screenshots
